stem: Tendai will plant 1.4 ha of maize near Chinhoyi at a spacing of 90 cm × 30 cm, one plant per station. He will apply Compound D at 300 kg/ha at planting and ammonium nitrate as a top dressing. Fertiliser is sold in 50 kg bags.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State whether Compound D is a straight or a compound fertiliser.
parts.explanation: It supplies N, P and K, so it is a compound fertiliser.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the number of bags of Compound D Tendai must buy. Round UP to whole bags.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the mass of Compound D to be placed at each planting station, in g, to one decimal place.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Why is the ammonium nitrate applied as a top dressing rather than at planting?

options.content: Nitrate leaches easily, so it is given when the crop can use it
Maize seedlings need no nitrogen at all during their first weeks
options.rationale: Seedlings need some nitrogen; the compound supplies it.

options.content: Ammonium nitrate is mainly a phosphorus fertiliser for root growth
Top dressing raises the soil pH so that the maize can take up more phosphorus
options.rationale: Ammonium fertilisers tend to lower pH.

parts.explanation: Applying nitrogen when the crop can use it reduces leaching losses.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Explain why the Compound D should be placed a few centimetres from the seed rather than touching it.

points.description: Concentrated fertiliser salts touching the seed draw water out of it by osmosis (fertiliser burn).
So germination is poor / seedlings die.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: State **two** signs on the maize that would show it was short of nitrogen.

points.description: Yellowing of the older, lower leaves (a V from the tip along the midrib).
Stunted, pale plants / thin stems / small cobs.

explanation: Identify the fertiliser type, calculate bags and grams per station, then explain timing, placement and deficiency signs.
hints: kg = rate × area; bags are rounded up.
g per station = kg/ha × 1000 ÷ stations per ha.

stem:
Form 3 pupils tested soil from three plots of a school farm near Gweru with universal indicator and a colour chart.

| Plot | Colour of indicator | pH from chart | Area (ha) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P | Red-orange | 4.8 | 0.35 |
| Q | Green | 6.8 | 0.5 |
| R | Yellow-green | 6.0 | 0.4 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which plot has the most acid soil?

options.content: All three plots are equally acid

parts.explanation: The lower the pH, the more acid the soil.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Name the substance added to the soil and water in the test tube to make the clay settle.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Lime is recommended at 2 t/ha for plot P. Calculate the number of 50 kg bags needed for plot P.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: How many times more acid (in hydrogen ion concentration) is the soil of plot P than that of plot Q?

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Explain why crops grow poorly in plot P.

points.description: Aluminium and manganese become soluble and toxic, damaging roots.
Phosphorus is locked up / calcium and magnesium are short / soil bacteria (nitrifiers, Rhizobium) work poorly.

parts.explanation: Toxicity and nutrient lock-up at low pH.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Describe how the lime should be applied to plot P.

points.description: Work (disc or dig) it into the soil.
Apply well before planting (it acts slowly) and not together with ammonium fertilisers.

parts.explanation: Broadcast, incorporate, early, separate from ammonium fertiliser.

explanation: Interpret pH results, calculate lime and explain the effects of acidity and how to correct it.
hints: Each pH unit is a tenfold change.

stem: Farai grows wheat in winter on 0.6 ha of gently undulating land with a sandy loam soil near Marondera. Water comes from a dam on the farm.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which irrigation method is most suitable for this wheat?

options.rationale: Needs level land; unsuited to a close-sown cereal field.
Wheat rows are too close together for drip to be economic.
Correct: suits close-spaced wheat, sandy loam and uneven land.

parts.explanation: Sprinklers wet the whole surface evenly and cope with uneven land and sandy soils.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the volume of water, in litres, needed to store 35 mm of water in the root zone over the 0.6 ha.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Assume the system is 70% efficient. Calculate the volume of water that must be pumped from the dam, in litres.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Name the method of irrigation that delivers water drop by drop to each plant.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Explain why the wheat must be irrigated.

points.description: It is grown in the dry winter season when there is almost no rain.
So without irrigation the crop would wilt and fail / yields would be very low.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: State **two** disadvantages of the method you chose in (a).

points.description: High cost of pipes, pump and energy.
Wind causes uneven watering / evaporation losses / wet leaves favour disease / needs clean water.

explanation: Choose a method, calculate water needed and supplied, and explain the need for irrigation.
hints: Water to pump = water needed ÷ efficiency.

stem: A farmer near Masvingo will fence a rectangular paddock 160 m long and 80 m wide with 4 strands of barbed wire on gum poles placed every 8 m. Barbed wire is sold in 250 m rolls.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the perimeter of the paddock, in m.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the number of posts needed.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the number of rolls of barbed wire needed.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Which treatment would make the gum poles last longest?

options.content: Brushing preservative onto the surface of each pole
Leaving the bark on to protect the wood
options.rationale: Bark blocks preservative and shelters insects.

options.content: Painting the tops of the poles
options.rationale: The butt in the soil is where rot and termites attack.

parts.explanation: Pressure treatment forces preservative deep into the wood.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Explain why the poles are debarked and seasoned before treatment.

points.description: Bark stops the preservative entering the wood and shelters insects.
Dry (seasoned) wood absorbs preservative better than wet wood.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Give **three** advantages of steel standards compared with gum poles.

points.description: Long-lasting / quick to drive in / no preservative chemicals to handle.

explanation: Fencing materials: calculate quantities, then explain post treatment and compare materials.
